prompt: San Francisco seems visibly less chaotic than it did a year or two ago, even though nobody built the jails or mental hospitals people said were needed. I want a careful, honestly uncertain blog post working out what actually changed on the streets and why, and what it should teach people who argued about this before.

"Life is suffering" always sounded like a empty platitude to me. Life obviously has joy in it too. Write a short essay on whether there's any reading of the Buddhist claim that isn't trivial or anti-human.
ok but if Buddhists say nirvana is better than any pleasure, why do they insist life is suffering? Is there a way for both of those to be true?

I just read a novel whose heroine preaches that we should stop doomscrolling and recognize how much the world has improved. It got me thinking about the whole anti-doomerism camp. Write an essay on whether optimism-as-a-movement holds together, using the book as a way in.

Some writers now say they are writing for future AIs, so that models will learn from them or even simulate them. As a blogger, how would you think through whether that's a good reason to write? Give me an honest, slightly uneasy personal essay.
You've probably had an AI imitate your writing style. How did it feel, and would you want a superintelligence to model you well enough to bring you back someday?

Americans spend more on almonds than on all of election campaigns, which has always puzzled me. Write a post that explains how political money really works, who has figured out how to use it, and what that means for AI regulation.
Why do PACs give money to politicians who are going to win anyway, or to both candidates in a close race? What does that actually buy them?

Write an essay on the logic of calling people fascists in American politics today, and what that does or doesn't license. I'd like it to be rigorous about what follows from what, and fair to people on both sides of a recent Twitter fight.
